X_EFW_E01_S01_VIS.text: Begin in ordinary work. Theo keeps drilling after everyone else has cleared out; Vark comes down expecting an argument about overtime and finds Theo genuinely afraid to stop. Strip all readouts, depth claims and invented physics. Vark's concern is simple: the shift is over, the rig sounds wrong, and Theo is going to get hurt. Theo cannot justify himself without admitting that he has dreamed this exact moment. The drill finally strikes something that does not sound like stone. The work lamps flicker. A dark form emerges from black bedrock. Theo recognizes it before he understands it. End on Vark realizing Theo knew it was there.

X_EFW_E01_S02_VIS.text: Rae is alone when an erased location begins appearing in the archive as if the record itself has remembered it. Do not present this as a sensor anomaly. The disturbing fact is that the place has no official history and yet the archive is quietly writing it back into existence. A restricted line appears beside it: REDLIN PROTOCOL. Rae knows neither the protocol nor the person, but the name strikes her with the sick familiarity of a word heard in sleep. Caelum enters because the Spire has received reports from Olyria-Prime. Rae uses ordinary paperwork and dry irritation to keep his attention away from the returning record. When he leaves, the forbidden location and Redlin reference remain. Rae realizes her private dreams and the institutional archive are remembering the same thing.

X_EFW_E01_S03_VIS.text: The buried object is the Desert Marker. Its wrongness comes from age, scale and Theo's recognition, not from behaving like a machine. Vark draws a practical line: nobody touches it until people arrive who know what they are looking at. Theo says there are no such people. Theo removes one glove and places his palm against the Marker. The trench disappears. We enter a complete but very brief historical image: a ruined battlefield beneath a broken sky, suspended in the last quiet moment before catastrophe. STARBREAKER stands at the center of it, unmistakably a person rather than an icon. He is exhausted, furious and committed. A stellar-scale force is held at the edge of release. Someone outside the frame has asked him to wait. Starbreaker looks toward that unseen person and says, 'You know what happens if I do.' Then the memory ends before the act. Do not show ancient Theo. Do not show Redlin yet. Vark sees only fragments: another sky, figures where no figures should be, a shadow crossing the trench. Theo returns to the present with his empty hand curled as though he had been holding something. He now knows one name without knowing how: Starbreaker.

X_EFW_E01_S04_VIS.text: Adrian arrives after the site has been cleared. Theo, injured and furious, demands that another person acknowledge what happened. Adrian deliberately keeps his eyes on Theo rather than the Marker. This is avoidance, not clinical examination. Theo notices. When Theo starts toward the Marker again, Adrian catches his wrist and tells him not to touch it twice. Adrian will not explain a mechanism. He says the first contact was enough for the forgotten history to recognize Theo. Theo asks whether Starbreaker was real. Adrian's composure breaks at the name. He answers only: 'Yes.' That one word is more frightening than a lecture. Adrian refuses to say why Theo knew the name or why he himself recognizes it.

X_EFW_E01_S05_VIS.text: Rae locks herself in the archive long enough to copy what is returning: names, erased routes, fragments of testimony and the REDLIN reference. She is not collecting measurements. Caelum forces his way in and orders her to surrender the copy. Rae asks the question that matters: why was this removed? Caelum never answers. He tells her she is risking her position, housing, access and reputation for something she does not understand. Rae replies that this is precisely why she cannot hand it back. At the door she says 'Redlin' aloud. Caelum flinches before he can stop himself. That is her proof.

X_EFW_E01_S06_VIS.text: Let the issue breathe. Theo sits on a cot while an overworked medic wraps his hand and tells him to stop moving. Vark has a paper incident form because the network is down. There is bad coffee. Someone outside complains about a missing boot. Their argument begins as workplace comedy and becomes serious when Vark admits what he saw during the memory rupture. He does not understand it and does not want to. Instead of reporting everything, Vark strips identifying details from the incident report. His reason is ordinary: he does not know what the Marker is, but he knows what institutions do when they decide something belongs to them.

X_EFW_E01_S07_VIS.text: Rae takes the copied material to the oldest part of the archive. Adrian is already there with a sealed physical volume. Do not make their exchange a contest of deductions. Rae's advantage is that she recognizes institutional concealment. Adrian's is that he has lived with the concealment longer. Rae says 'Redlin.' Adrian does not answer. She shows him the old evacuation mark from her dreams. He reacts. Adrian tells her the archive is not incomplete by accident: some history was deliberately removed. Rae asks what everyone was afraid of. Adrian refuses to answer and instead asks when she first dreamed the mark. When Rae refuses, he tells her she already knows enough to be in danger.

X_EFW_E01_S08_VIS.text: Theo returns to Sector Four ahead of an official patrol and starts dragging spoil and wreckage over the exposed Marker. He is injured, clumsy and running out of time. Adrian watches until Theo finally asks for help. Make Theo say why: he spent years wanting proof he was not imagining things; now that proof exists, he is afraid of who will claim it. Adrian helps conceal the site. A patrol passes. Adrian uses ordinary envoy authority, not impossible technical tricks, to send them toward the officially reported collapse. Theo realizes Adrian could have intervened earlier. Adrian says the dangerous question is no longer what the Marker is, but who the forgotten history recognizes.

X_EFW_E01_S09_VIS.text: Rae waits with the copied material. Caelum appeals first to loyalty, then to fear. He tells her she can still surrender it and return to ordinary life. Rae asks him to say the erased place-name and then Redlin's name. He will not. That refusal makes the decision for her. Rae destroys the copy. Caelum's anger is not that data is lost; it is that the forbidden knowledge now survives inside Rae instead of inside an institution he can control. He warns her that others will come for what she remembers. Rae leaves before they can.

X_EFW_E01_S10_VIS.text: Theo has finished burying the Marker when he notices Adrian preserved a small record of the site. Theo confronts him with an industrial cutter, hands shaking. Adrian sees fear rather than competence. Theo wants the location erased. Adrian refuses to promise because the location is no longer the important fact. Theo asks what recognized him. Adrian says he does not know. That admission matters. Adrian knows history and consequence, not the operating rules of reality. Before leaving, Adrian tells Theo: if this were only buried matter, none of them would be afraid.

X_EFW_E01_S11_VIS.text: Rae returns to the archive and destroys the remaining trail connecting her identity to the recovered material. Adrian arrives after the damage is done. He does not congratulate her. He points out the cost: she has cut herself away from the institution that gave her access, status and protection. Rae says it was a job, not a life. Adrian breaks the identification crystal that would let the Spire follow her. When Rae asks where she is supposed to go, he tells her somewhere she has never dreamed of. The wording reveals that he knows the dreams are real. He says she is not the first person to remember something history says never happened.

X_EFW_E01_S12_VIS.text: Night above Sector Four. Theo sits alone with a small fragment he kept from the Marker. He turns it in his injured hand because he cannot let go of the first physical proof that the visions exist outside him. Adrian appears and tells him to put it down. Theo asks whose memory he is seeing. Adrian says he cannot answer; Theo hears both inability and refusal. The fragment warms. Theo hears the distant sound of an orbital canopy breaking over a city that no longer exists. Adrian reacts before he can hide it. Theo realizes Adrian knows that sound. Theo asks whether Adrian remembers the same sky. Adrian finally says yes. Do not reveal that Theo was present in the ancient scene. End on the terrifying relief of knowing the impossible history is shared—and the worse realization that Adrian knows why.
